transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, um... I guess I'm here because I'm just always moving from one thing to the next. I can't really just sit idle. And, uh, they changed things up at work recently, so... it's just been a lot harder to hide it.
How far back do you remember feeling like you always had to be moving or doing something? Was this something you noticed about yourself as a child, or did it start more recently?

Um... I guess it's been a long time. Way before this recent job change. 

I suppose... even back in grade school. I remember my teachers used to write that I was bright, but... careless. And that I'd talk out of turn. They always had to remind me to just stay with my work. So... yeah. Since I was a kid.
When you're trying to focus on something, like reading or working on a task, do you find it hard to keep your attention on it, or do you get distracted easily?

Yeah... I suppose so. Um, like at work. I have the chat window, the CRM, team messages... they're all open at once. If there's a beep, or... if a coworker is talking nearby, I just get pulled off track. I end up losing where I was with the customer. So... yeah.
Have you ever had periods where you felt unusually happy, energetic, or 'on top of the world' for several days in a row, even when things weren't going particularly well?
Um... no. Not really. I don't think I get like that. Just... normal, I guess.

Do you find yourself doing things without thinking them through first, or acting on impulse? For example, interrupting people, making quick decisions you later regret, or doing risky things without considering the consequences?

Um... I suppose I do interrupt sometimes. I don't mean to be rude, but... if I hear coworkers trying to work through a customer problem, I'll just jump in with an answer. Usually before they've finished, or... before anyone even asked me. So... yeah, I guess that happens.

How much do these difficulties with attention and impulse control affect your daily life? For instance, do they cause problems with your relationships, your work performance, or how you feel about yourself?

Um... well, it affects work, I suppose. It's... it's been coming up in my reviews lately. My supervisors, they... they point out unfinished tickets, little mistakes I make. They say it slows the team down. I mean, I try hard, and... I get along fine with the customers, mostly. But... yeah. It causes some problems there.
When you were a kid in school, did your teachers or parents ever say you were fidgety, restless, or that you couldn't sit still? Or did they mostly just complain about you not paying attention?

Um... I suppose it's been going on a long time. Long before this job change, anyway. Back in grade school... my teachers used to write that I was bright, but careless. And... that I talked out of turn. They always had to remind me to just stay with my work. So... yeah. Both, I guess.

When you're sitting at your desk trying to work, do you find yourself fidgeting a lot — like tapping your fingers, bouncing your leg, shifting around in your chair — or does it feel like you need to get up and move around?

Um... I guess so. I mean, I try to look calm, but... my foot is usually bouncing under the desk. Or... I might be clicking a pen during a meeting. I don't really notice I'm doing it until someone looks. But... yeah, I suppose I fidget.
When you think back to your earliest memories of school — like first or second grade — were you already having trouble sitting still and paying attention, or did that start a bit later on?

Um... well, like I mentioned a little bit ago... it was pretty early on. Grade school. That's when the teachers were already writing those things... about me being careless, and talking out of turn. So... yeah. It started back then.
When you were in first or second grade, roughly how old would that have been for you?

Um... I guess I would have been around six or seven. Like I said before, it was a long time ago... way before this new job. My teachers were already saying I was bright but careless back then... and that I talked out of turn and needed reminding to stay on task. So... yeah, early grade school.

From grade school all the way through to now, has this difficulty with attention and restlessness been pretty constant... or have there been times — like months or years — where it got much better or pretty much went away?
Um... I don't know. It's just... always been there, I guess. I haven't really kept track of it. It's just how things are.
Outside of work — like when you're at home, with friends, or doing hobbies — do you notice the same kinds of problems with focus and fidgeting, or is it mainly just at work?

Um... I guess it's at home, too. It's not just work. Like... if I try to do quiet stuff, things that are supposed to relax me. Reading, or... trying to sit through a movie with my wife. It usually doesn't last long before I'm shifting around, or... making comments, or just getting up to do something else. So... yeah.

Requires further assessment of symptom onset, duration, context, and functional impact.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with lifelong history of inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity dating to early grade school (age 6-7), with persistent symptoms across multiple settings (work, home, leisure). Core ADHD symptoms confirmed: difficulty sustaining attention, distractibility by environmental stimuli, fidgeting/restlessness, impulsive interruptions, and functional impairment in work performance. No evidence of manic episodes or other mood disorders. Symptom onset before age 12 and chronic course support ADHD diagnosis. F90.9 (ADHD, unspecified type) selected as hyperactivity-impulsivity vs. inattentive presentation is not definitively distinguished, though both are evident.
